# Henry Vu (full)

Machine learning engineer at eXRealityAI in Dallas, Texas, and an M.Sc. student in
Computer Science at the University of Texas at Dallas, expected Summer 2027. This file is the
complete text of https://henryvu.io/ for language models and search engines.

## About

Hey, I'm Henry. I'm a machine learning engineer at eXRealityAI in Dallas, and I'm finishing my M.Sc. in Computer Science at UT Dallas,
expected Summer 2027. Before that I did my B.Sc. Honors in Computing Science at the University of
Alberta.

At eXReality I build XR Auto Service and Smart DVI, a spatial AI platform for auto shops. It puts
an agent on a technician's headset that guides them through a repair or an inspection and answers
questions from a repair knowledge graph. I also work on inference at the edge, running voice and vision models locally on NVIDIA
Jetson and Apple silicon, and I shipped GardenXR to the Meta Horizon Store. On the research side,
I work with Dr. Katherine Brown at UT Dallas on NIH-funded ultrasound segmentation, getting models
small and robust enough to run on portable hardware.

On the research side I work with Dr. Katherine Brown at UT Dallas on NIH-funded ultrasound
segmentation, and earlier I did online algorithms and bandits at Amii. I write about all of this
at henryvu.blog.

## Where I've worked

### Founding Machine Learning Engineer at eXRealityAI, Aug 2025 to now

- Built the knowledge graph and retrieval layer behind a Meta Quest 3 automotive repair app for an
  OEM pilot, and the evaluation harness that scores it in CI. On an expert-written test set it puts
  the correct procedure first 92 percent of the time.
- Built a voice-to-voice assistant that runs entirely on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin: Whisper for speech
  in, hybrid BM25 and FAISS retrieval, a quantized Mistral 7B, and Kokoro for speech out.
- Multimodal XR workflows on Gemini, YOLOv9, and Wit.ai voice input across two applications, and a
  retrieval pipeline (EmbeddingGemma, cross-encoder reranking, query rewriting) that cut retrieval
  work by roughly half.
- Shipped GardenXR to the Meta Horizon Store, traced a run of bad production answers to a vendor
  proxy that was silently dropping images, and mentored the team on LLM integration.

### Computer Vision Engineer at ThorMed Innovation, Feb 2025 to now

- Modeling lead on an NIH-funded project to segment the bladder in clinical ultrasound, so patients
  can be monitored without a catheter.
- Pretrained U-Net and SimSiam encoders on 9.2K ultrasound images before fine-tuning, reaching
  96 percent Dice.
- Got the model onto portable hardware with 4-bit quantization, where the domain-pretrained weights
  held up about seven times better than ImageNet weights, and built the pipeline that extracts and
  cleans frames from clinical ultrasound video.

### Teaching Assistant at UT Dallas, Jan 2025 to now

- Algorithms and data structures: weekly office hours, seminar and exam material, and technical
  reviews for more than a hundred students.

### Undergraduate Research Assistant at SODALab, Dec 2023 to May 2024

- A theoretical and empirical survey of multi-armed bandits across stochastic, adversarial,
  Markovian, and restless settings, with Dr. Xiaoqi Tan.
- Simulations comparing UCB, Exp3, Thompson sampling, and the Gittins index.

### Teaching Assistant at the University of Alberta, Sep 2023 to May 2024

- Algorithms and data structures for a few hundred students: office hours, weekly problem-solving
  sessions, and grading.

### Undergraduate Researcher, Online Learning, at Amii, Apr 2022 to May 2023

- Online optimization with the primal-dual framework: conversion, knapsack, and bipartite matching
  problems where decisions are made before all the input arrives.
- Algorithms that use machine-learned predictions to beat worst-case bounds when the predictions
  are good, without losing the guarantees when they are not.

## Projects

- XR Auto Service. Hands-free, step-by-step diagnostics and repair guidance for automotive
  technicians on a headset, built by Henry at eXRealityAI. https://exreality.ai/xr-auto-service.php
- Smart DVI. AI-guided digital vehicle inspection with hands-free photo and video capture, voice
  input, and an advisor-ready report, built at eXRealityAI. https://exreality.ai/smartdvi.php
- DatDai. A question-answering assistant over Vietnamese land law, live on Cloud Run. Every answer
  cites the exact article and clause, an amendment graph pulls in the decrees that later changed a
  clause, and a citation verifier checks each cited article against what was actually retrieved,
  with no extra model call. Python, Gemini, Qdrant, Langfuse, Cloud Run.
  https://github.com/HenryVu27/DatDai
- ADHD Coaching Agent. A coaching chatbot for parents of children with ADHD: a LangGraph ReAct agent
  between two guardrail gates, hybrid retrieval with a local cross-encoder reranker, four-tier
  memory, and an evaluation package with LLM judges and pairwise comparisons. Python, LangGraph,
  Qdrant, ONNX. https://github.com/HenryVu27/ADHDAgent
- GardenXR. A mixed-reality gardening app for Meta Quest, published on the Meta Horizon Store after
  passing review for restricted camera access. Twenty thousand people used it in the first two
  days. Unity, C#, Gemini. https://www.meta.com/experiences/gardenxr/24200709416226235/
- Ultrasound Bladder Segmentation. NIH-funded work with UT Dallas Bioengineering: self-supervised
  pretraining on 9.2K ultrasound images, then 4-bit quantization for portable devices, with a paper
  on making the models small and robust. PyTorch, SimSiam, U-Net.
  https://github.com/HenryVu27/ThorMed and
  https://github.com/HenryVu27/ThorMed/blob/main/Thormed_ISBI_New.pdf
- ML Interview Practice. LeetCode-style practice for ML coding interviews that runs entirely in the
  browser: real CPython with numpy through Pyodide, no backend, no build step. Built in eight days
  before an interview and used for real. JavaScript, Pyodide, CodeMirror.
  https://henryvu.io/MLInterviewPractice/ and https://github.com/HenryVu27/MLInterviewPractice
- Agentic Framework for Suspect Detection. Multi-agent pipeline using LangGraph and Gemini for
  automated suspect identification from surveillance data. Python, LangGraph, Gemini, FAISS.
  https://github.com/HenryVu27/Suspect-Detection
- StitchKit. Turns a client's logo into a machine-ready embroidery stitch file for a one-person
  shop whose only computer is an older iPhone: phone-first, entirely in Vietnamese, with preflight
  checks because a bad file perforates leather for good. Python, FastAPI, Ink/Stitch, Swift.
- VoiceBridge. Real-time Vietnamese-to-Russian speech translation over push-to-talk, a two-day
  proof of concept for a director who needed to talk across a language barrier. FastAPI, Deepgram,
  DeepL. https://github.com/HenryVu27/voice-agent
- EEG Decoding: a Multi-Modal Approach. EEG signal classification that fuses convolutional features
  and self-attention with language-model embeddings, with a paper.
  https://github.com/HenryVu27/EEG-Multimodal-Decoding
- Modeling Political Sarcasm. Detection models using feature engineering and a fine-tuned
  DistilRoBERTa to identify subtle political sarcasm in online text.
  https://github.com/HenryVu27/PoliticalSarcasm
- Multi-armed Bandits and Online Learning. Survey, simulations, and seminar slides from the Amii and
  SODALab work. https://github.com/HenryVu27/Multi-armed-Bandits-and-Online-Learning
- Polyps and Breast Ultrasound Segmentation. Attention U-Net for medical image segmentation on
  polyps and breast ultrasound datasets. https://github.com/HenryVu27/Polyps-Segmentation
- A Survey of Geometric Set Cover. Approximation algorithms and PTAS approaches for the geometric
  set cover problem. https://github.com/HenryVu27/Geometric-Set-Cover

### Earlier work

BTS Concert Ticket Buying Simulator (2026), Valentine Surprise (2026), TFT Rolling Odds
Calculator (2025), This Web Portfolio (2024), UManitoba Navigator (2024), ViT and Contrastive
Representation Learning (2023), VAE and Diffusion for FashionMNIST (2023), Yahoo's News
Recommendation with MABs (2023), Gomoku Solver (2022), Online Algorithms seminar slides (2022),
HabiTrak (2021), Toronto Neighbourhoods Data Analysis (2021), Sudoku Solver (2020), Edmonton
Restaurant Finder (2020), Encrypted Arduino Communication (2019), Huffman Coding for File
Compression (2019).

## Frequently asked

Who is Henry Vu? A machine learning engineer at eXRealityAI in Dallas and an M.Sc.
student in Computer Science at the University of Texas at Dallas, expected Summer 2027. He also
works as a computer vision engineer at ThorMed Innovation on NIH-funded medical imaging, and
graduated summa cum laude from the University of Alberta.

What does Henry Vu work on? Knowledge graphs, retrieval, and evaluation for LLM products; voice
and vision models running at the edge on NVIDIA Jetson; mixed reality apps for Meta Quest; and
self-supervised learning and quantization for medical ultrasound segmentation. Earlier, online
algorithms and multi-armed bandits at Amii and SODALab.

Where does Henry Vu work? eXRealityAI, where he builds XR Auto Service and Smart DVI;
ThorMed Innovation, as a computer vision engineer on NIH-funded bladder segmentation; and UT
Dallas, as a teaching assistant for algorithms and data structures.

What has Henry Vu built? The knowledge graph, retrieval layer, and CI evaluation harness behind a
Meta Quest 3 automotive repair app; a voice-to-voice assistant that runs entirely on an NVIDIA
Jetson Orin; GardenXR, published on the Meta Horizon Store; DatDai, a Vietnamese land-law
assistant on Cloud Run with a citation verifier; an ADHD coaching agent with guardrails and an
evaluation suite; and ML Interview Practice, a browser-only Python practice site.

Where did Henry Vu study? B.Sc. in Computing Science with Honors, summa cum laude, from the
University of Alberta, and an M.Sc. in Computer Science at the University of Texas at Dallas,
expected Summer 2027.

What is Henry Vu's blog about? Deep-dive technical content at henryvu.blog about AI engineering
(context engineering for LLMs, RAG systems, agent architectures), ML systems, and reinforcement
learning (multi-armed bandits), aimed at practitioners who build real ML systems.
